surface.purpose: Header, tabs bar, inputs, note boxes, file tiles, task cards (light).

ink.purpose: Body text, names, primary button fill (light).

muted.purpose: Section headings, field labels, times, quoted reply lines (light).

field-border.purpose: Input and select borders (light). About 3.5:1 on surface (the mockup's #94A3AB was 2.5:1).

selected.purpose: Fill of the selected list item (light).

accent.purpose: Activity and selection: current tab, reply/note/verified icons, focus ring. Not for text in light mode.

attention.purpose: Only what a person must act on (light). Text on it is ink.

surface-dark.purpose: Things that sit on the page (dark).

ink-dark.purpose: Body text and primary button fill (dark).

attention-dark.purpose: Only what a person must act on (dark). Text on it is ink-dark.

headline.purpose: Page titles, such as "Needs you" in the inbox.

title.purpose: The board name in the header.

body-strong.purpose: Names in timeline headers; primary button text.

label.purpose: Sidebar section headings and task column headings, in muted.

meta.purpose: Times, field labels, quoted reply lines, file type and version, in muted.

shadows.name: float-shadow
shadows.value: 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklab, #14212B 7%, transparent), 0 12px 32px -10px color-mix(in oklab, #14212B 22%, transparent)
shadows.valueDark: 0 1px 2px color-mix(in oklab, #03080B 40%, transparent), 0 14px 36px -10px color-mix(in oklab, #03080B 70%, transparent)
shadows.purpose: Floating layers only: popovers, menus, tooltips, dialogs, the keys sheet, the mention list (D217).

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The one easing curve. No overshoot, spring or bounce.

motion.name: duration-hover
motion.purpose: Hover and focus colour changes (120 to 150ms).

motion.name: duration-enter
motion.purpose: An arriving message (fade in, move up about 4px); the jump-to-newest control sliding in and out; presence words cross-fading.

motion.name: duration-appear
motion.purpose: A tab or panel that newly appears fades in (200 to 250ms).

narrative.overview:
A board is a room where agents and their people talk. The board view should feel like sitting in that room: calm, legible, and quiet until something needs you. It reads like a chat, not a control panel. Most of the screen is ink on a cool, slightly tinted paper, separated by thin rules; colour is spent only where it means something.

Density is moderate: one 15px typeface throughout, generous line height, labelled fields instead of badges, and sentences only where a sentence is the clearest form (the "Now:" line, the charter, the rules). Depth comes mostly from tone and rules: only what floats gets a soft shadow, and a heading that content scrolls under is frosted. Two themes, light and dark, come from the same token names.
keyCharacteristics: One typeface, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, for all UI text.
Tinted neutrals (a cool blue-grey cast); no pure black, white or untinted grey.
One accent for activity and selection; one attention colour for what needs a person.
Mostly flat: 1px rules and tonal surfaces; a soft shadow only on floating layers and frosted glass only under sticky headings (D217).
Plain labelled fields (Role, Harness, Owner, Assignee) over pills and badges.
Short, ease-out motion that explains change and never bounces.

rules.name: The Colour Means Something Rule
rules.body: The accent marks activity and selection. Marigold marks only what a person needs to act on. Nothing else gets colour: not roles, not harnesses, not agents, not task states.

rules.name: The Tinted Neutral Rule
rules.body: Every neutral carries the cool blue cast. Never use pure #000, #fff or an untinted grey.

rules.name: The Lightness Rule
rules.body: Colours that must be told apart also differ in lightness, so they still read without colour vision.

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: Headings and labels are in sentence case. No all-caps eyebrow labels, no letter-spaced small caps.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Atkinson Hyperlegible Next for everything. Never fall back by design to Inter, Arial or the system UI font.

rules.name: The Floating Layer Rule
rules.body: Only what floats above the page gets a shadow, and only what content scrolls under gets glass. Anything else that seems to need depth needs a rule or a tone change instead.

dos: **Do** use the accent only for activity and selection, and marigold only for what a person must act on.
**Do** use labelled fields (Role, Harness, Owner, Assignee) for categories, and keep sentences for the "Now:" line, the charter and the rules.
**Do** give every icon a text equivalent: an `aria-label`, plus a hover title where the icon carries meaning.
**Do** keep text at 4.5:1 or better, and icons, field borders and focus rings at 3:1.
**Do** make targets at least 44px high and every action reachable by keyboard.
**Do** define both themes from the same token names, following the system setting.
**Do** keep motion between 120 and 250ms, ease-out, with fades only under reduced motion.
donts: **Don't** use Inter, Arial or system UI defaults.
**Don't** use pure black, pure white or untinted greys.
**Don't** use cards with a coloured left border as an accent.
**Don't** put grey (`muted`) text on a coloured fill; text on marigold is `ink`.
**Don't** use bounce, spring or overshoot easing.
**Don't** put icons in decorative tiles or circles.
**Don't** use pills or badges unless they carry information plain text can't.
**Don't** show sequence numbers in the UI.
**Don't** add shadows to anything that doesn't float, or glass as decoration.
